newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH CONSITUTION NOT PROBLEM FOR EMU -NIINISTO.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH CONSITUTION NOT PROBLEM FOR EMU -NIINISTO.

text.p: Finnish Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto said on Wednesday he did not expect constitutional issues to pose any major problem for Finnish membership of European economic and monetary union (EMU).

"There is a constitutional aspect ... but I do not believe it makes any major problem when we are talking just (about) entering (EMU)," Niinisto told Reuters Financial Television (RFTV) in a live interview.

"I see that we are capable of entering the third stage with a simple majority," he said, referring to parliament's vote due early in 1998 on Finnish membership of the single currency, which would precede voting on necessary constitutional changes.
"I think that ... the members of parliament will very carefully study the case and after that they will be ready to join EMU," Niinisto said.
The constitution says unequivocally that the Finnish currency is the markka. By joining EMU, Finland must at the latest in 2002 replace the national currency with the euro.
This will require legislation in so called constitutional order, which means a two-thirds majority in parliament.

Niinisto reiterated the government's view that Finland already meets all entry criteria for EMU, but underlined that the public deficit and debt were bolstered by healthy social security fund surpluses and that state debt was still rising.
"The central government debt will be just slightly over 70 percent," he said, referring to debt in relation to GDP. State debt to GDP was 69.5 percent in 1996.
State debt servicing costs would go on rising into next millennium, Niinisto told RFTV.
"It will be bigger than now up to the beginning of 2000," he said. In the 1997 budget approved by parliament state debt servicing amounts to 26.8 billion markka, or 14 percent of total expenditure.
"Around 2002-2003 we could make a surplus in the state budget and that means that the interest (costs) would start to go downwards," Niinisto said.
